ideas.name: KineticID
ideas.problem: The discrepancy between custom client motion guidelines (specific easing curves, velocity, and color palettes) and the actual animation execution, which leads to brand inconsistency and costly revision cycles.
ideas.targetUser: Freelance motion designers and boutique animation studios managing high-volume production for enterprise clients with strict kinetic brand standards.
coreFeatures: Brand Curve Profile Importer (Bezier/Ease-in-out presets)
Visual Easing Curve Overlay & Comparison Tool
Motion-Color Compliance Scanner
Automated Brand-Match Scoring Engine
Client-Ready Validation PDF Export
realDependencies: Lottie/Bodymovin JSON parser for keyframe data extraction
Figma REST API for real-time brand color/style synchronization
AWS S3 for storing client motion-identity profiles
FFmpeg for frame-by-frame velocity analysis of rendered video
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local `brand_profiles.json` to simulate a database of client identities (e.g., 'TechSlick' vs 'PlayfulPop'). File uploads will be simulated using a 3-second `setTimeout` accompanied by a 'Parsing Keyframes...' progress bar. Instead of actual Lottie parsing, the app will ingest a hardcoded `mock_export.json`. The 'Compliance Score' will be calculated by a function that compares the hardcoded mock values against the selected brand profile, adding a +/- 3% random jitter to make the results look like authentic, real-world measurement data.

ideas.name: LingoLens
ideas.niche: Visual-first localization context for indie game development
ideas.problem: The 'blind translation' gap where translators work in spreadsheets without seeing the UI, leading to text overflow (e.g., German words being too long) and semantic errors (e.g., mistaking a button label for a descriptive sentence).
ideas.targetUser: Solo indie developers and freelance localization managers who need to ensure UI integrity across multiple languages without requiring translators to have full access to the game engine.
coreFeatures: Visual Context Overlay: Upload UI screenshots and automatically overlay translated strings onto their intended positions.
Dynamic Overflow Detection: Real-time visual warnings (red highlighting) when a translated string exceeds the pixel dimensions of its designated UI container.
Semantic Tooltip Previews: Hover over a string to see the 'source' context, including the original English text and a screenshot of the specific UI element.
Side-by-Side Language Comparison: Toggle between multiple target languages on the same UI mockup to instantly compare spatial impact and layout shifts.
realDependencies: Cloud Storage API (AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage) for hosting high-resolution UI assets
TMS API Integration (Lokalise, Phrase, or Crowdin) to sync real-time translation data
JSON/CSV/XML Parsing Engine for ingesting standard game localization files
Canvas-based Image Rendering Engine for dynamic text-on-image manipulation
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local directory of static PNG UI mockups (Main Menu, HUD, Inventory) and a hardcoded 'mock_strings.json' file that simulates a TMS database. API calls to 'Sync with Lokalise' will be intercepted by a middleware that triggers a 2.5-second loading spinner before returning a successful response with mock data. Overflow detection will be emulated using a simple character-count-to-width heuristic: if a string's length exceeds a specific threshold defined in the mock JSON, the UI will render a red bounding box around the text to simulate a layout break.

ideas.name: FluxSpatial
ideas.niche: Visual planning and spatial interaction logic mapping for XR/VR developers.
ideas.problem: The 'invisibility' of interaction volumes (hitboxes, proximity triggers, and grab zones) leads to inconsistent user experiences, high debugging costs, and 'interaction friction' where players feel objects are unresponsive or broken.
ideas.targetUser: Technical artists, XR level designers, and gameplay engineers working in Unity or Unreal Engine who need to validate interaction ergonomics and trigger logic before high-fidelity implementation.
coreFeatures: 3D Spatial Heatmap Overlay to visualize trigger density and collision volumes
Node-Based Interaction Logic Editor for mapping spatial events to actions
Automated Friction Simulator using 'Ghost Hand' playback paths to detect dead zones
Direct Engine-Ready Metadata Export (JSON/XML) for Unity and Unreal integration
realDependencies: Unity/Unreal Engine Plugin API for real-time scene synchronization
OpenXR standard for spatial coordinate mapping
USD (Universal Scene Description) for complex environment importing
Cloud-based collaboration API for shared interaction design
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will load a pre-packaged .glb environment representing a typical VR room. Interaction zones will be rendered as semi-transparent colored meshes. A 'Simulated Player' will be an automated, path-following 'Ghost Hand' that moves through the scene; success or failure of interactions will be determined by basic Euclidean distance math between the ghost hand and object nodes. API calls such as 'Export to Engine' or 'Sync Scene' will trigger a mock progress bar with a randomized 1.5s to 3s delay and a subsequent 'Sync Complete' notification. The logic editor will function via a mock JSON state object that validates connection paths visually without running a real physics engine.

ideas.name: PulseArc
ideas.niche: Music production arrangement and energy management
ideas.problem: The 'mid-track slump'—producers struggle to maintain momentum and emotional flow, leading to tracks that feel repetitive, structurally weak, or lack clear tension and release dynamics.
ideas.targetUser: Bedroom and semi-professional electronic and pop producers (ages 18-35) who use DAWs like Ableton Live, FL Studio, or Logic Pro and struggle with long-form composition and structural cohesion.
coreFeatures: Interactive Energy Canvas: A drag-and-drop timeline to plot intensity points (0-100) to create a visual wave.
Genre-Specific Blueprint Templates: Pre-built structural curves for styles like Melodic Techno, Future Bass, or Pop.
Element Layering: A secondary track layer to map specific elements (e.g., Kick, Lead, FX) against the energy curve.
Tension/Release Heatmap: A visual overlay that highlights 'slump zones' where tension is too low for too long.
Exportable Arrangement Blueprints: High-res image or PDF exports to be used as a visual guide alongside the DAW.
realDependencies: Firebase Auth for user account management
AWS S3 for storing user project JSON files and exports
Stripe API for premium template subscriptions
Librosa (Python) or Essentia (C++) for audio-to-energy automated curve generation
ideas.emulationStrategy: Use a MockService singleton that returns Promises with randomized latency (400ms - 1500ms) to simulate network requests. Authentication will be simulated via a 'fakeLogin' method that returns a hardcoded user object after a delay. Data persistence will be handled via 'localStorage' to mimic a database, allowing 'projects' to be saved and reloaded. The 'Auto-Analyze' feature will be emulated by a 3-second loading animation followed by the injection of a randomized array of values with high variance into the canvas, simulating the analysis of a complex audio file.

ideas.name: Proofframe
ideas.niche: The workflow gap between academic research and visual storytelling for long-form video creators.
ideas.problem: Video essayists face extreme cognitive load when trying to synchronize dense scholarly citations with specific video timestamps, leading to 'source drift' where visual claims become unverified or difficult to credit during the editing process.
ideas.targetUser: Professional and semi-professional documentary-style video essayists (10k-1M+ subscribers) who produce 20+ minute deep-dives requiring high levels of factual accuracy and multi-source attribution.
coreFeatures: Dual-Pane Evidence Sync: A split-view interface that links research snippets (text/PDF highlights) directly to specific video timestamps in a media player.
Citation-Linked Storyboard: A drag-and-drop timeline where every visual 'beat' is hard-linked to a bibliographic entry, ensuring a clear audit trail from claim to evidence.
Automated Bibliography Export: A one-click engine that converts storyboard citations into formatted APA/Chicago/MLA lists for video descriptions and end-credit rolls.
Semantic Asset Tagging: A tool that scans research notes and suggests relevant clips from the user's local media library based on conceptual similarity.
realDependencies: Google Drive/Dropbox API for cloud-based research file access
Zotero/Mendeley API for academic citation management integration
YouTube Data API for pulling and timestamping existing video footage
OpenAI API (Embeddings) for semantic search between notes and video metadata
AWS S3 for high-resolution video clip hosting and previewing
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'MockServiceLayer' that intercepts all API calls. File access will be simulated via a local 'assets/' folder containing three sample PDFs and five short MP4 clips. Network latency will be simulated using a randomized `setTimeout` between 400ms and 1500ms for every interaction to mimic real API calls. The 'AI semantic search' will be faked using a simple keyword-matching algorithm against a local `mock_knowledge_base.json` file. A 'Connection Status' indicator will toggle between 'Connected' and 'Syncing...' to enhance the realism of the asynchronous data fetching.
